This week’s read · 2026-07-29 (cached)

The headline allocation posture holds at -0.16 (CAUTION, 75% exposure) with neither pillar delivering enough to break the standoff — and both open questions from the previous brief are set to resolve within the next 24 hours. On the market side, growth impulses posted their first positive daily tick in several sessions, rising +0.04 to -0.46 as oil pulled back modestly, and Trump's statement that there is a "good chance" of progress in Iran talks is the first concrete diplomatic marker toward a Hormuz resolution, but neither development is large enough to push market momentum past the +0.25 LONG threshold on its own. Meanwhile the economy side has softened further: Atlanta Fed GDPNow printed its final Q2 estimate at 1.5%, one more tick lower, and consumer confidence slipped to 90.8 for its third straight monthly decline; the macro buffer holds at +0.48 because labor markets remain solid and inflation is dormant, not because underlying demand has stabilized. Microsoft and Meta report after the bell tonight. With beat probabilities already priced above 90%, the real test is capital-expenditure guidance and whether AI spending is visibly converting to revenue — a confident outcome would firm breadth, currently the strongest component at +0.62, and could push market momentum through the LONG threshold; a cautious outlook or a miss would likely keep it pinned. The BEA advance Q2 GDP estimate and June personal consumption data follow tomorrow morning: a print near GDPNow's 1.5% confirms soft growth but leaves the macro buffer intact if inflation stays quiet, while a deep miss paired with consumer prices showing early tariff pass-through would be the first real challenge to the buffer's durability and raises the risk of a move toward CASH. The dashboard's call is clear: hold CAUTION, nothing is broken, and the path to LONG opens if tonight's earnings and tomorrow's data deliver rather than disappoint.

1How the index has evolved

Milk Road Macro Index (MRMI)

How it's built: MRMI combines MMI (market momentum from credit, breadth and volatility) with a macro buffer that erodes when growth and inflation both deteriorate. The formula is unchanged; the production posture layer maps MRMI to RISK-ON, CAUTION, or RISK-OFF.

Reading the chart: amber line is the MRMI value over time. Green zone = RISK-ON above +0.25, amber = CAUTION from −0.50 to +0.25, red = RISK-OFF below −0.50. Toggle assets in the legend to overlay SPX / Russell / BTC.

2What the markets are signalingMarket pillar

MMI — Market Momentum Index. The fast, market-derived half of MRMI: built entirely from price and volatility data — credit spreads, cyclical sector breadth, and financial-conditions volatility — equally weighted. Markets react quickly, so MMI catches turning points early; the trade-off is they can also flash false alarms, which is why MMI alone never triggers a RISK-OFF call. It only acts in concert with the slower economy pillar below.

Market Momentum Index (MMI)

What you're seeing: the MMI score over time, equally-weighted from GII (global growth momentum), Breadth (cyclical participation) and FinCon (financial conditions). Above zero = healthy momentum. Below zero = momentum is rolling over.

Drivers below: click any row to expand the underlying series. The MMI score is just the average of the three.

Market momentum on its own, averaged from credit spreads, sector breadth and financial-conditions volatility.

This week’s read · market pillar · 2026-07-29 (cached)

Market momentum sits at +0.11 for a second straight session — flat on the day (+0.00) but down -0.33 over the week — stuck in CAUTION territory and -0.14 short of the LONG threshold. Growth impulses registered their first positive daily tick in several sessions, rising +0.04 to -0.46, as a modest pullback in oil prices gave the supply-shock indicators a brief reprieve; the physical disruption is still live — Houthi attacks on Red Sea tankers continue and oil remains above $100 — but Trump's July 28 statement that there is "a good chance" of progress in Iran talks, with Omani mediators hoping to signal movement within days, is the first concrete diplomatic marker that the dashboard's weakest component might have a recovery path. Breadth slipped one tick to +0.62 but holds as the firmest leg of the three; seven of eleven S&P 500 sectors closed higher on July 28, with staples, discretionary, and communication services leading while tech and energy lagged — a rotation pattern that supports a broadly held market even when mega-cap technology is under pressure. Financial conditions were essentially unchanged at +0.18 — VIX edged down to 18.21 from 18.67 yesterday, MOVE held at 70.88, and high-yield spreads at 2.81 barely moved — which tells you credit markets are still treating this as a manageable geopolitical shock rather than a systemic one. The week's damage is real (-0.33 on market momentum, -0.35 on growth impulses, -0.36 on financial conditions), but the rate of daily deterioration has slowed sharply compared to last week, suggesting the worst of the supply shock's impact on the dashboard may already be priced in. The score won't recover in earnest without growth impulses turning positive, which requires oil retreating further from triple digits or a concrete Hormuz agreement; Microsoft and Meta report after the bell tonight, and the previous brief's watch-point has arrived — AI-monetization beats with confident guidance would firm breadth and could push market momentum through the LONG threshold, while a miss or cautious capital expenditure guidance would likely keep it pinned in CAUTION.

3What the economy is signalingEconomy pillar

Macro Stress. The slow, economy-derived half of MRMI: built from real-economy data — consumer spending, jobs, income, GDP nowcast — and inflation trajectory. The unified 0–10 score is calm by default, rises when either growth weakens or inflation accelerates, and builds fastest when both factors hit together.

Macro Stress

What you're seeing: Martin's unified macro-stress score on a 0–10 scale. It is calm by default, rises when growth weakens or inflation accelerates, and builds fastest when both hit together.

MRMI buffer: this same stress score now erodes the macro buffer used in the production MRMI strategy.

MACRO STRESS INPUTS · Real Economy Score · Inflation Direction Δ6m — click any row to expand
This week’s read · economy pillar · 2026-07-29 (cached)

The macro stress score sits at +0.48 — Calm on the 0–10 scale — with the macro buffer at +0.48, near-full strength and still holding the headline posture intact as tomorrow brings the most consequential data in weeks: the BEA Q2 advance GDP estimate and June personal income and spending drop simultaneously on July 30. The open question from the last brief has not resolved, and the evidence running up to it keeps pointing soft: Atlanta Fed GDPNow printed its final Q2 nowcast at 1.5 percent on July 28, another tick lower from last week's 1.6% and 0.8 percentage points below the Econoday consensus of 2.3%, with the move driven by cuts to private investment estimates. That revision came after June's advance goods trade deficit narrowed to $101.5 billion, but the improvement reflected falling imports rather than stronger exports — a pattern that boosts the GDP calculation without saying anything useful about underlying demand. Conference Board consumer confidence fell to 90.8 in July, the third straight monthly decline, with the Present Situation component dropping 3.6 points as households reported worsening views on business and labor conditions. Those reads keep the real economy score at -0.64 (+0.04 on the week), still in mildly negative territory and unchanged in character since the soft patch began. Inflation still adds no stress: the inflation direction axis is flat at +0.00 for a second consecutive week, core CPI holds at 2.60% year-over-year, and the five-year breakeven at 2.16 shows markets are not pricing in tariff pass-through. A GDP print at or below GDPNow's 1.5% final read tomorrow would confirm the soft-growth regime rather than resolve it; what actually begins eroding the +0.48 macro buffer is a specific double hit — that GDP miss paired with June PCE data showing consumer prices reaccelerating, the combination that turns the inflation direction axis positive and tests the framework in earnest for the first time.
